New study sets independent switch demands at input, output and motor levels, compares current human EEG/behavior with fitted hierarchical diffusion parameters; source does not introduce de novo Frank PBWM nor physiologically prove BG/PFC causation.

source_specific_negative_and_limitations.claim: Across full model, none of overall error rate main effects reached significance (F1,29<3.11), even where RT main effects did.
Updating-only switch RT shows ONLY output-gating significant main effect; input/response switch RT main effects F1,29<1.1 nonsignificant.
All pairwise RT under-additive interactions survive on updating trials, but update-only 3way F1,29=2.74 p=.21 does NOT.
Updating errors no switch main effects or other two-way interactions; input×response and 3way only significant.
Input/output/response error main effects significant, but among interactions only input×response was significant; condition dependence.
HDDM posterior predictive fit is imperfect (especially some long RT/QQ tails); same-time case empirical distributions are not identical to model posterior predictive.

source_specific_negative_and_limitations.locator: original S4 Fig visual, original Discussion
source_specific_negative_and_limitations.claim: Drift rate varies with task processing/gating in addition to inferred threshold; exclusive a-only mechanism unsupported.
EEG scalp GLM pattern/decoding does not directly observe dopamine, BG or causal PFC gate or uniquely distinguish neural latent mechanics.
Parallel and under-additive gating are functional interpretations, not exhaustive proof against alternative simultaneous or time-varying dynamic diffusion accounts.
